reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel sigma-algebra, U:E->R twice continuously differentiable, and nonnegative real m<=b with m||w||^2<=D2U(x)[w,w]<=b||w||^2 for all x,w. For real A,d with A>0,d>0,d=dim_R E, and every fixed u in E, define F(x)=U(x)+||x-u||^2/(2A), a=m+1/A,c=b+1/A,k=c/a,T(x)=x-(1/c)grad F(x). T^n is n-fold iteration including T^0(v)=v. N(v) is the least natural n with ||grad F(T^n(v))||^2<=d/A when such an n exists, and zero otherwise; xp(v)=T^N(v)(v). Then a,c>0 and k>=1; grad F(x)=grad U(x)+(x-u)/A for all x; N and xp are measurable. For every v: ||grad F(xp(v))||^2<=d/A; ||u-A grad U(xp(v))-xp(v)||=A||grad F(xp(v))||; that residual is <=sqrt(dA); every natural j<N(v) has d/A<||grad F(T^j(v))||^2; N(v)<=Nat.ceil(k log(1+A||grad F(v)||^2/d)); and real N(v)+1<=k log(1+A||grad F(v)||^2/d)+2. For every probability measure mu on E and every real M, if v->||grad F(v)||^2 is Bochner integrable under mu and its integral<=M, then real N+1 is Bochner integrable and integral(N+1)dmu<=2+k log(1+AM/d).
